summary: Private SAML: IdP metadata EntityID namespacing mismatch triggers auth redirect loop
description: Issue summary: After onboarding Nimbus Health's private deployment (VPC) and configuring SAML with their IdP, users are unable to complete authentication: browser repeatedly redirects between Redwood Console and the IdP SSO endpoint. Impact: All interactive login flows fail for users authenticating via SAML; API token exchange for service accounts also times out. Environment: Private control plane (v1.8.2) deployed in customer VPC, prod | us-west-2. Customer IdP: ADFS fronted by Azure AD SAML proxy. Steps to reproduce: 1) Navigate to customer console SSO login URL. 2) Select enterprise SSO. 3) Redirect to IdP, complete primary auth. 4) Instead of returning to Console with a SAMLResponse POST, browser is redirected back to IdP login URL (loop). Observed logs: authn flow shows repeated 302 -> SAMLRequest generation -> IdP metadata mismatch error in Redwood Auth service logs. Error snippet: "Received SAMLResponse for unknown EntityID 'https://login.nimbus.local/saml/metadata' (expected namespaced id https://nimbus-prod.login.nimbus.local/)". Past attempts: re-uploaded metadata, regenerated SP certificate, rotated ACS URL mapping. None resolved loop.
steps_to_reproduce: Open Redwood private console URL for Nimbus Health
Complete IdP primary auth and observe redirect loop back to IdP
logs: auth-service[pid=1823]: WARN SAML: incoming EntityID 'https://login.nimbus.local/saml/metadata' does not match stored SP mapping 'https://nimbus-prod.login.nimbus.local/'
proxy[pid=2001]: DEBUG forwarding SAMLRequest to idp.nimbus.health:443
console[pid=1500]: ERROR failed to set session after SAML auth: revalidation failed
comments: 2025-02-12 09:40 - Lina Cortez (Support): Created ticket after customer reported immediate failures post-metadata-update.

2025-02-12 10:15 - Rajat Singh (SRE): Initial triage: reproduced redirect loop in staging private cluster by spoofing IdP EntityID. Hypothesis: IdP is presenting a non-canonical EntityID due to internal DNS rewrite/proxy. Requesting IdP metadata file from customer.

2025-02-12 11:30 - Nimbus Health (Customer): Provided IdP metadata and noted that the proxy rewrites hostnames for multi-tenant routing. Customer confirms they updated metadata earlier today as part of a rollout.

2025-02-13 08:05 - Rajat Singh (SRE): Confirmed mismatch between IdP metadata EntityDescriptor entityID and the AssertionConsumerService/SingleSignOnService hostnames. Filed INT-1182 to add tolerant matching for namespaced hostnames in SP mapping logic.

2025-02-14 14:22 - Eng/Identity (Anika Patel): Investigated authentication library. Observed strict equality check on entityID; adding a configurable canonicalization step could resolve but needs review. Draft PR referenced.
2025-02-15 09:10 - Nimbus Health: Tested temporary workaround (replacing stored SP mapping to match non-canonical entityID). Confirmed users can now complete auth and login sessions are established.
investigation_notes: Reproduced redirect loop by configuring IdP metadata with bare hostname (login.nimbus.local) while the SP mapping expected namespaced hostname (nimbus-prod.login.nimbus.local).
Auth service currently compares entityID strings exactly; no normalization for subdomain prefixes or tenant namespaces.
Proxy in front of IdP rewrites URLs for routing to tenant-specific backends; this produces a different entityID in the metadata served at runtime than what customer uploaded earlier.

Workaround validated: temporarily updating SP mapping in Redwood Console to accept the IdP's current EntityID allows flow to complete. Not ideal for long term as customer intends to restore canonical hostnames.
Customer cannot immediately change proxy behavior due to HA constraints and firewall rules.
resolution_notes: Temporary workaround applied: Support updated SP EntityID mapping to accept the IdP's non-canonical EntityID; customer confirmed restored login flows (2025-02-15).

Engineering change required: implement entityID canonicalization (strip tenant prefixes and optionally support regex-based matching) and expose a UI toggle to accept non-canonical metadata for Private deployments.

INT-1182 created to track infra/service change. Linked PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/6421 contains prototype canonicalization logic; requires security review and QA on private deployments before rollout.

Follow-ups: 1) Security review to ensure relaxed matching doesn't introduce cross-tenant SSO risks. 2) Update Private deployment onboarding runbook to call out proxy/DNS impacts on IdP metadata. 3) Offer short-term managed change: Redwood can host an IdP metadata translation proxy for Nimbus Health if they cannot alter their proxy.
